correctness.rationale: For odd \(k\), exact \(2\)-adic valuation gives \(2^{n+v_2(n)}\mid y-1\), contradicting the size of \(y^k=n2^n+1\) for \(k\ge3\). For even \(k\), writing \(z^2=n2^n+1\) and halving \(z-1,z+1\) gives coprime consecutive factors; all powers of two lie in the even factor, forcing an inequality impossible for \(n\ge4\). The remaining values give exactly \(9\) and \(25\).

value.rationale: This is a natural complete intersection problem for a classical named integer sequence and the standard class of perfect powers. The primary Cullen literature explicitly motivates searching for Cullen numbers with other structured properties. The result is an unrestricted classification, not a bounded census; it upgrades a known square boundary to all exponents.
